newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says no cabinet reshuffle for time being.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says no cabinet reshuffle for time being.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh reaffirmed on Tuesday that he would not reshuffle his cabinet for the time being as rumoured in the media.
He also blamed unidentified parties for spreading rumours of a reshuffle to try to undermine the country's economy, which is already undergoing a severe downturn.

Chavalit's statement follows speculation that some members of his six-party coalition were seeking the removal of his finance minister, Amnuay Viravan, who has been trying to put the economy back on track.
Thailand's economy has braked sharply this year and private economists see economic growth falling to between three and five percent in 1997 from 6.4 percent in 1996.

Troubles have also hit the depressed and cash-strapped finance and property sectors, exports have turned sluggish, high interest rates are stifling business activity, the baht is the target of speculative attacks and the stock market has sunk to eight year lows.
Coalition sources had said that Chavalit had been pressured by some in the government to launch a cabinet reshuffle and that Amnuay was one of the targets.
"There is no pressure at all," Chavalit told reporters when asked if some coalition partners were asking him to reshuffle his cabinet.

"And there will be no change in the cabinet line-up for the time being. I will urge my fellow ministers to help me in an effort to stop these destructive rumours on a cabinet reshuffle," he said after the weekly cabinet meeting.
"The Prime Minister told the cabinet during the meeting that there will be no cabinet reshuffle, no change of the people who are in charge of the finance ministry."
Political sources said the Chart Pattana Party (CPP), the second largest party in the six-month-old coalition government, has been at odds with Amnuay's handling of the economy.
On Monday, Amnuay said he had no plans to quit despite the talk that he may be pressured to leave.
